entry.title: Intel 8087 Tangent Algorithm Implementation Details
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | righto.com | discussion | hacker news

The 8087 floating-point coprocessor uses a hybrid algorithm to compute the tangent function (FPTAN) with high speed and 64-bit accuracy. The approach combines the CORDIC algorithm for initial angle reduction with a Padé approximant—a rational polynomial—to compute the remaining small angle.

Through microscopic analysis of the chip's circuitry and microcode ROM, the process was identified as a three-stage sequence: pseudo-division to generate CORDIC decision bits, calculating a rational approximation, and pseudo-multiplication to perform rotations. This specific implementation avoids slow division operations, enabling significantly faster computation than the 8086 microprocessor.

This prevents the instability of local secrets or remote attestation quotes that would otherwise break when legitimate system changes, such as kernel updates, alter standard PCR values.

Lobsters Top | kdeforpeople.com | discussion

A community of KDE users and contributors is urging the KDE Project to implement a ban on generative AI within the Plasma Desktop and its components. The group argues that the technology undermines code review, compromises user privacy, and introduces human rights concerns that current proposals fail to adequately address.

The proposed restrictions would cover AI-generated outputs in code, assets, merge request descriptions, issues, and translations. Supporters state the ban is necessary to maintain developer trust and to align the project's development practices with the ethical goals of KDE Eco.

entry.title: Digital Signatures Proposed for Mesh Networks as Alternative to Encryption
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | andanti.no | discussion

Mesh network protocols could use digital signatures for sender authentication while maintaining cleartext message transmissions. This approach aims to facilitate use within amateur radio bands, where total encryption is often prohibited but verifying the identity of transmitters is necessary for regulatory compliance and network management.

The design offers benefits like increased network transparency and easier filtering of unauthorized users, but faces challenges including higher bandwidth overhead for signatures, potential loss of privacy, and the need for a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) to manage authentication.

entry.title: Loris Cro Outlines the Zig Programming Language Journey
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | kristoff.it | discussion

Loris Cro, VP of Community at the Zig Software Foundation, outlines a three-tiered approach for developers using the Zig programming language. The framework suggests that newcomers should prioritize understanding target systems over high-level frameworks, intermediate users should focus on designing code behavior and dependency management, and advanced users should aim for full functional completeness and project ownership.

The advice, shared during a speech at Zigtoberfest, advocates for a systems programming philosophy that emphasizes direct control over hardware and dependencies. This approach is designed to help developers transcend high-level abstractions and become more effective engineers by maintaining a deep understanding of the underlying machine.

entry.title: Radicle Discloses Critical Network Protocol Vulnerabilities
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | radicle.dev | discussion

Radicle has disclosed two critical security vulnerabilities in its network protocol affecting all released versions. The flaws permit attackers to read data in transit due to a lack of encryption and allow for peer impersonation through broken connection handshakes.

Users are advised to stop using private repositories over the network and rotate any exposed credentials until a fix is released. A planned major update will resolve the issues by migrating to the iroh networking stack, a change that will be backward-incompatible and will result in a network partition between upgraded and non-upgraded nodes.

entry.title: Parsing JSON Without Intermediate ASTs
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | arthi-chaud.github.io | discussion

Parsing JSON objects in Haskell without an intermediate representation (IR) or Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) is possible through the use of partially-initialised data. This technique employs `undefined` for fields in the target data structure and uses a bitset to track which fields are populated during parsing to ensure all required data is present.

Bypassing the IR minimizes memory allocation and computational overhead, significantly accelerating deserialisation. Benchmarks demonstrate that this approach can be approximately three times faster than the standard `aeson` library, though it requires non-strict data types and increased implementation complexity.

entry.title: GitHub Wiki Use Critiqued as Documentation Anti-pattern
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | michaelheap.com | discussion | hacker news

Maintaining project documentation in a `/docs` folder within a repository is presented as a superior alternative to using GitHub's built-in wiki feature. Using a dedicated directory allows documentation to be versioned alongside the codebase, enabling peer reviews through standard pull request workflows and automated linting via GitHub Actions.

The author recommends using GitHub Pages to host the documentation and treating the wiki as a simple redirection tool. This approach ensures that documentation remains accessible locally when a repository is cloned and supports professional tooling and branding.

entry.title: The Strategic Risks of Abandoning Scientific Linux
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | blog.melashri.net | discussion | hacker news

The author argues that CERN and Fermilab's decision to retire Scientific Linux in favor of CentOS was a strategic error because it eliminated the institutional capability to maintain an independent, RHEL-compatible operating system. While intended to reduce redundant engineering efforts, the move removed the "option value" provided by an independent distribution—the ability to maintain a credible, independent alternative if upstream providers like Red Hat changed their development models or licensing.

The utility of such independence became evident when Red Hat's pivot to CentOS Stream forced large-scale users to seek alternatives like AlmaLinux. Furthermore, CERN's planned migration of over 2,200 accelerator control systems to Debian 13 by 2026 highlights the importance of distribution portability in ensuring long-term hardware compatibility that newer RHEL versions may no longer support.

entry.title: Jev-style Decision Logic Implemented in Python
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | nobodywho.ai | hacker news

A 25-line Python script mimics the behavior of decision-only "System One" models like TypeSafe AI's Jev. Using `llama-cpp-python` and `numpy`, the script loads a GGUF model and extracts logit probabilities for predefined labels to enable fast, local classification.

The implementation distinguishes simple local probability extraction from sophisticated production models that utilize synthetic data and Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD) to achieve calibrated outputs.

entry.title: SAML Design Flaws and the Case for Deprecation
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | blog.trailofbits.com | hacker news

SAML is an XML-based authentication protocol facing significant security challenges due to its inherent complexity and design flaws. Its reliance on XML makes implementations vulnerable to several attack classes, including XML Signature Wrapping (XSW), canonicalization errors, and parser differentials.

The transition toward modern, transport-aware protocols like OpenID Connect (OIDC) highlights SAML's "kitchen-sink" design and lack of alignment with contemporary web standards. The protocol's complexity and historical baggage suggest it is a candidate for deprecation in favor of more streamlined and secure authentication frameworks.

entry.title: AMD Zen 5 RDSEED Bug Causes Non-Random Zero Returns
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | board.flatassembler.net | source | hacker news

The AMD Zen 5 architecture contains a hardware bug in the RDSEED instruction that causes the random number generator to return zero at an inconsistent rate. This flaw can incorrectly signal a successful operation even when the entropy is not truly random, potentially resulting in predictable cryptographic keys.

The vulnerability, cataloged as CVE-2025-62626, was addressed via security bulletin AMD-SB-7055. While testers have observed the issue in various software environments, AMD has confirmed the flaw and noted that microcode updates are required to maintain hardware randomness integrity.

entry.title: Learning Serious Text Editors Requires Significant Time and Effort
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | utcc.utoronto.ca | discussion

Mastering tools like GNU Emacs or Vim requires a substantial investment of time and effort. Because these editors offer complex extensibility and unique interaction models, achieving true fluency is a significant project rather than a simple skill acquisition.

Switching between editors often necessitates relearning workflows and duplicating established configurations. While basic `vi` knowledge is recommended for Unix sysadmins, the steep learning curve of new software suggests that users should stick with a functional editor once they have found one that works.
